reasons: internal/adapters/smtp/client.go:156-158 `authenticate` wraps every `c.Auth` error in `*AuthError` unconditionally, so the deadline/ctx-close this PR newly arms on the AUTH exchange (client.go:122-123) surfaces as `smtp auth: read tcp ...: i/o timeout` → Send returns `SendError{temp:false}` (client.go:244-247) → `applySendResult` marks the outbound `failed` with no retry (internal/application/send.go:461). A relay that stalls after `AUTH PLAIN` is exactly the transient condition this PR exists to make retryable, yet it is the only leg that ends permanent. Reproduced with fakeRelay(hangAfter:"AUTH", ehlo:["AUTH PLAIN"]), CommandTimeoutSec=1: elapsed 1.01s, Temporary()=false. The scout note claiming 'classify treats non-textproto as temp so the result is temporary' is false for AUTH because that path never reaches classify.

Fix (keep the 5xx-reply rule intact): in `authenticate`, wrap as `*AuthError` only when `errors.As(err, &*textproto.Error)` (a real server reply such as 535); for any other error return it plain (and pass it through `s.cause` at client.go:123-126 so a ctx cancel during AUTH is annotated like the other legs). Add a `TestSendCommandTimeout` case with `relayOpts{ehlo: []string{"AUTH PLAIN"}, hangAfter: "AUTH"}` and `sendOpts(port, "plain", "u", "p")` asserting `Temporary()==true`, `errors.As(err,&*AuthError)==false`, `strings.Contains(err.Error(),"timeout")` and elapsed < 4s; the existing 'rejected credentials are a permanent AuthError' (client_test.go:323) must still pass. Note the fakeRelay `hang(command)` gate fires after the AUTH line is read and before the 235/535 reply, which is the right hang point.
notes: Verified: the five new TestSendCommandTimeout cases fail (hang → test timeout after 30s) with origin/main's client.go swapped in and pass on the PR (go test -race, 4.4s); go build ./..., go vet, gofmt -l clean; probe file removed and working tree restored clean.

Verified the Uncertain rule holds: deadline after DATA hand-over yields net.Error.Timeout → isConnectionLost → Uncertain (test covers it); ctx close there gives net.ErrClosed → also Uncertain; AuthError-on-535 and Password.Zero semantics unchanged; no new config key, no migration, no auth/authz/route change, no secret in error text (net errors carry only addresses).

Resource handling: every connect error path closes conn and detaches the AfterFunc; success paths use defer s.close(); double close in TestConnection (Quit then close) is harmless. context.AfterFunc closing the conn concurrently with net/smtp is safe (net.Conn is goroutine-safe).

Not verified: STARTTLS leg only relies on tls.Conn delegating reads to the raw conn whose deadline is set (existing TestSendSTARTTLS passes but no silent-after-STARTTLS test); a slow-link large-DATA scenario was only checked for intact delivery on loopback. Neither is a blocker.

Test hygiene (non-blocking): 'ctx cancel unblocks a stuck command' calls got.waitHung(t) → t.Fatal from a non-test goroutine; vet did not flag it because the call is indirect, but if the relay never hangs the failure will be reported oddly. Consider signalling on a channel and asserting in the test goroutine.
Scope is tight (smtp adapter + two callers + one domain field), fully revertable by git revert.
